title: BJP holds Save Democracy march in Thane

tea.why: The BJP organised the march to protest against what it described as increasing lawlessness, mob rule, and attempts to create anarchy.
tea.want: The party stated the march aimed to protect democratic institutions, uphold the Constitution, and maintain law and order.
tea.changed: Nov 1: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis addressed the rally, accusing the Congress party of subverting democratic institutions.

summary: On November 1, 2026, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) held a 'Save Democracy' march in Thane, Maharashtra. The event, which began at Parmarth Niketan in Pachpakhadi and concluded at Talao Pali, was organised to protest against what the party described as rising lawlessness and mob justice. Senior BJP leaders, including Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav, and state president Ravindra Chavan, participated in the rally. During his address, Chief Minister Fadnavis criticised the Opposition, alleging that they were attempting to destabilise the country and subvert the Constitution. He further stated that the march marked the beginning of a sustained struggle against forces he claimed were creating chaos. No specific demands were issued beyond the stated goal of protecting democratic institutions and the Constitution.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The BJP announced plans to hold a 'Save Democracy' march in Thane on November 1.
The march took place in Thane, featuring speeches from senior BJP leaders including Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.
